figure_caption: Protocol overview. Comparison rows from four evaluation designs are fit with a ridge Bradley--Terry model. Rows are ordered by their one-step influence on the decisive margin: leader vs. runner-up for top-1, or the $k$-th vs. $(k{+}1)$-th player for a top-$k$ set. The shortest prefix whose removal or outcome reversal changes the target is found by exponential and binary search. Every probe is an exact refit, and the final set is re-verified independently. Sizes are reported as a count $\hat{k}$ and as a fraction $\hat{k}/n$. A random-subset comparator, a direct leader--challenger heuristic, a planted-minimum control, a row-permutation control, and seed replay calibrate the instrument.

panels.title: What is perturbed: rows, estimator, target
panels.short_caption: Comparison rows (a, b, y) from four evaluation designs are dropped or flipped; a ridge BT fit defines the top-1 / top-k target and the decisive pair L vs C.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: Comparison rows from four evaluation designs are what gets perturbed; a ridge Bradley–Terry fit turns them into a ranking whose top-1 or top-k set (and decisive pair L vs C) is the tested target.

LAYOUT (portrait panel, flows top -> bottom in three stacked bands):

Band 1 — "Evaluation designs" (top, ~40% height). A group container titled `Four evaluation designs`. Inside, five compact source cards stacked vertically (sharp-cornered data boxes), each card = small icon slot on the left + source name + a tiny right-aligned tag. Group the cards into four design sub-groups with a thin design label on the left edge of each sub-group:
  - design `Crowdsourced votes`: card src_arena: `Chatbot Arena` · tag `top-5` ; icon [[pl: small crowd of people voting thumbs-up icon]]
  - design `Expert annotation`: card src_mtb_h: `MT-Bench experts` · tag `top-3` ; icon [[pl: small person-with-clipboard expert icon]]
  - design `LLM judge`: card src_mtb_g: `MT-Bench GPT-4` · tag `top-3` ; icon [[pl: small robot judge icon]]
  - design `Sports`: two cards src_nba14 `NBA 2014` · tag `top-5`, and src_nba15 `NBA 2015` · tag `top-5` ; one shared icon [[pl: small basketball icon]]
Below the five cards, a one-line strip `3 cases each: drop/top-1 · flip/top-1 · drop/top-k`.

Band 2 — "Comparison rows" (middle, ~30% height). Edges from every source card converge (solid arrows, unlabeled, merging into one bus arrow) into node rows: a data table drawn as a sharp-cornered stacked-rows table (4–5 visible rows, then an ellipsis row) with column headers `a` `b` `y`. Example row cells: `3 | 7 | 1`, `5 | 2 | ½`, `7 | 1 | 0`, `…`. Table title: `Comparison rows  r = (a, b, y)`. Small legend beside it: `y ∈ {1, ½, 0}` (win / tie / loss). To the right of the table, two small perturbation glyphs, stacked, each with a dashed arrow pointing INTO the table (these are the perturbations acting on rows):
  - pert_drop: a row strip with a strike-through / X glyph, label `Drop` and sub-label `delete rows`
  - pert_flip: a row strip with a circular swap arrow glyph, label `Flip` and sub-label `y ↦ 1−y`
These two glyphs are emphasized — they answer "what is perturbed".

Band 3 — "Estimator and target" (bottom, ~30% height). Solid arrow rows -> bt_fit. bt_fit: rounded process box `Ridge Bradley–Terry fit` with a small second line `λ = 0.1`. A small sharp side-badge attached to bt_fit: `p×p sufficient stats  W, N`. Solid arrow bt_fit -> ranking. ranking: a vertical mini leaderboard (sharp data box) of 6 ranked bars labelled by rank `1`…`6` with score symbol `θ̂` above it. On the ranking, mark two things:
  - target_top1: a bracket around rank 1 labelled `top-1`
  - target_topk: a bracket around ranks 1–k labelled `top-k set`
  - decisive pair: rows k and k+1 highlighted as a pair, with labels `L` and `C` and a small vertical double-arrow between them labelled `margin m`.
Next to the ranking, a small result-styled node target: `Target changes?` with sub-label `C overtakes L` — this is the test condition re-used in the next panel; give it an outgoing solid arrow to the right edge of the panel (hand-off to the search panel), labelled `θ̂, L, C, m`.

panels.title: Influence-ordered search, verified by exact refits
panels.short_caption: Rows are sorted by first-order influence on the margin; exponential + binary prefix search probes each candidate with an exact refit, and the final set is re-verified, giving k̂ and k̂/n.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: Rows are ordered by first-order influence on the decisive margin, and the shortest changing prefix is found by exponential + binary search in which every probe is an exact BT refit — the linear approximation only orders, the refit certifies.

LAYOUT (widest panel; three stages left -> right on the top half, search trace + verification on the bottom half; overall a clockwise U-shaped flow).

Top-left — stage 1 `Influence ordering`. Incoming solid arrow from the left panel edge labelled `θ̂, L, C, m`. Rounded process box infl: `One linear solve` with symbol `$$v = H^{-1}(e_L - e_C)$$` as a small label beneath. Directly under it, THE ONE EQUATION OF THE FIGURE, in a highlighted equation box eq_delta (two terms side by side):
  `$$\Delta^{\text{drop}}_r = -(y_r - p_r)(v_{a_r} - v_{b_r}) \qquad \Delta^{\text{flip}}_r = (1 - 2y_r)(v_{a_r} - v_{b_r})$$`
This is the single most novel element; it must be the only multi-term equation in the whole figure.

Top-center — stage 2 `Sorted rows`. Solid arrow infl/eq_delta -> sorted. sorted: a horizontal strip of ~14 small row tiles (sharp data cells) sorted by ascending Δ_r, with a graded encoding from "most margin-shrinking" (left) to "least" (right); an axis arrow beneath the strip labelled `ascending Δ_r`. A bracket over the first several tiles labelled `prefix D_s` (length s). Small note-free tag at the strip's left end: `most margin-shrinking`.

Top-right — stage 3 `Exact refit`. Solid arrow sorted -> refit labelled `perturb D_s`. refit: rounded process box `Exact refit` with second line `damped Newton on W, N`, a small badge `warm start θ̂` and a small badge `‖∇‖ < 10⁻¹⁰`. Solid arrow refit -> test. test: decision diamond `Target changed?`. Dashed feedback arrow from test back to sorted labelled `next s` (the search loop). This loop is emphasized: every probe passes through Exact refit.

Bottom (spanning width) — search trace search_plot: [[mp: qualitative search trace. x-axis "prefix length s" on log2 scale (ticks 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, no numeric emphasis); y-axis "refit margin" with a horizontal dashed zero line labelled "target changes below 0". A smooth decreasing curve (gently non-monotone wiggle allowed) starting positive and crossing zero between s=32 and s=64. Doubling probes at s=1,2,4,8,16,32,64 drawn as open circles with a small label "exponential"; subsequent bisection probes between 32 and 64 drawn as filled dots converging on the first crossing, labelled "binary". Mark the crossing point with a vertical tick labelled "k̂". Every probe marker represents one exact refit. Minimal ticks, no grid, no legend box; qualitative only.]] Place it below stages 2–3, with a thin connector from test (on `yes`) into the plot's k̂ marker region. Left of the plot, two small labelled stage tags stacked: `Exponential search  s = 1, 2, 4, …` and `Binary search` with sub-label `O(log k̂) refits`.

Bottom-right — certification chain. Solid arrow test -> found labelled `yes`: found: result-styled box `Shortest changing prefix`. Solid arrow found -> reverify: rounded process box `Independent re-verify` with sub-label `evaluator refit`. Solid arrow reverify -> report: result box (emphasized, the panel's output) `Verified size  $$\hat k$$` with two sub-fields side by side: `count  $$\hat k$$` and `fraction  $$\hat k / n$$`. Under report, a small badge `upper bound  $$\hat k \ge k^\star$$`.

IMPORTANCE: (1) Exact refit + loop + Independent re-verify (verification is the point), (2) eq_delta + sorted strip with prefix bracket, (3) report box k̂ / k̂/n, (4) search trace plot.

EDGES: input -> infl (solid, label `θ̂, L, C, m`); infl -> eq_delta (solid, short); eq_delta -> sorted (solid); sorted -> refit (solid, label `perturb D_s`); refit -> test (solid); test -> sorted (dashed, label `next s`); test -> found (solid, label `yes`); found -> reverify (solid); reverify -> report (solid). If test->sorted feedback crosses another edge, the two crossing edges take distinct colors.

panels.title: Comparators and controls
panels.short_caption: Random-subset and direct-heuristic comparators plus planted-minimum, row-permutation and seed-replay controls (and pre-search gates) calibrate the instrument.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: The same data are run through two comparators and three validity controls (plus pre-search gates) that calibrate the instrument across all 15 real cases of the four designs.

LAYOUT (portrait panel; a central instrument node with calibration blocks stacked above and below; flows top -> bottom).

Top — node instrument: compact rounded process box `Influence search + exact refit` with a small `$$\hat k$$` output port, representing the instrument from the centre panel (incoming solid arrow from the left panel edge, unlabeled). Beside it a small sharp data badge cases: `15 real cases · 4 designs`.

Block A — group container `Comparators` (same data, same verified prefix search). Two side-by-side cards, each a rounded process box with a tiny icon glyph and a one-line sub-label:
  - cmp_random: `Random subsets` · sub-label `≥ 10 of 20 subsets change` · glyph: a few scattered dots (random picks among row tiles)
  - cmp_heur: `Direct heuristic` · sub-label `leader's wins removed first` · glyph: a row strip with the leftmost tiles struck through
Both cards send solid arrows into a shared small summary node ratio: `clipped log₂ ratio` with symbol `$$\log_2(k_{\text{cmp}}/\hat k)$$` and a tiny sub-label `bootstrap CI over cases`. A solid arrow from instrument into ratio as well (the k̂ it is compared with).

Block B — group container `Validity controls`. Three stacked cards, each = icon glyph + name + one short sub-label, with a check-mark slot on the right (result-styled):
  - ctl_planted: `Planted minimum` · sub-label `3-player synthetic, brute-force k*` · glyph: triangle of three player dots
  - ctl_perm: `Row permutation` · sub-label `Arena rows reordered → same k̂` · glyph: two row strips with crossing shuffle arrows
  - ctl_seed: `Seed replay` · sub-label `seeds 101 / 102 / 103 · output hash` · glyph: circular replay arrow
Dashed arrows from instrument to each control card (auxiliary checks), unlabeled.

Block C (bottom, thin strip) — group `Pre-search gates` as three small inline chips (sharp boxes) in one row: `non-degenerate margin  m > 10τ`, `empty perturbation: no change`, `reversed-order refit = θ̂`. A short solid arrow from this strip up to instrument labelled `pass`. (If this arrow crosses a dashed control arrow, the two crossing edges take distinct colors.)

IMPORTANCE: (1) Comparators block (random subsets, direct heuristic), (2) Validity controls block, (3) instrument node, (4) pre-search gates strip.
